history.text: The city's roots are traced to the winter of 1879, when a group of miners ignored pleas by Frederick Pitkin, Governor of Colorado, to return across the Continental Divide to avoid a Ute uprising.
The Aspen, Colorado, post office opened on June 7, 1880.

history.label: 1880s
history.text: Waite, an Aspen newspaperman and agitator, was elected governor of Colorado on the Democratic ticket, but in time the movement failed. Railroads During the silver boom of the 1880s, two railroads raced to reach.
Pitkin County was created on February 23, 1881, with Aspen as its first and only seat.
Despite these setbacks, the Colorado Midland ultimately completed the line, and in early February 1888, the first Midland train arrived in Aspen.
In its peak production years of 1891 and 1892, Aspen surpassed Leadville as the United States' most productive silver-mining district.

history.label: 1930s
history.text: Aspen's development as a ski resort began in the 1930s when investors conceived of a ski area, but the project was interrupted by World War II.
The Aspen Skiing Company was founded in 1946 and the city quickly became a well-known resort, hosting the FIS World Championships in 1950.
Paepcke also played an important role in bringing the Goethe Bicentennial Convocation to Aspen in 1949, an event held in a newly designed tent by the architect Eero Saarinen.

history.label: 1970s
history.text: In the 1970s, Aspen became known as a playground for the rich and famous.

history.label: Modern city
history.text: Originally named Ute City, the small community was renamed Aspen.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: In the same week, the Denver and Rio Grande completed its line into Aspen, becoming the first railroad to provide direct rail service to the town.

history.label: Regional role
history.text: The move was led by Terry Paulson, an Aspen City Council member, and supported and guided by national groups such as the Carrying Capacity Network, and the Center for Immigration Studies.

sectors.name: Snowmass
sectors.summary: 98 trails over 3,342 acres, served by 20 lifts
sectors.text: The largest of the four and the one with its own village, built for long days and mixed-ability groups.

sectors.name: Aspen Mountain
sectors.summary: 115 trails over 828 acres, served by 8 lifts
sectors.text: Known locally as Ajax, it rises straight out of downtown Aspen and is best suited to intermediate and expert skiers - beginner terrain is limited.

sectors.name: Buttermilk
